:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Calculate $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{\sin x}\left(\cot x + \sin^2 x\right)\,\textrm d x.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity $\dfrac{1}{\sin x } = \csc x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}(\operatorname{cot}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡x+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/key-prerequisites.:topic/title: Simplifying Expressions Using Basic Trigonometric Identities

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{tan}⁡x(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x+2\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity ${cot}^{2}⁡x=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}({cot}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}+\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int ({csc}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1) \\  & =1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity  $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /15}^{0}8\operatorname{sec}⁡5x(\operatorname{tan}⁡5x-{cos}^{2}⁡5x)\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{-\pi /15}^{0}(\operatorname{sec}⁡5x\operatorname{tan}⁡5x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡5x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{\int }_{-\pi /15}^{0}(\operatorname{sec}⁡5x\operatorname{tan}⁡5x-\operatorname{cos}⁡5x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=5x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.$ 

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=5x.$

| $x$ | $-\frac{\pi }{15}$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\frac{\pi }{3}$ | $0$ |

Therefore, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}8{\int }_{-\pi /15}^{0}(\operatorname{sec}⁡5x\operatorname{tan}⁡5x-\operatorname{cos}⁡5x)\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{0}(\operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u-\operatorname{cos}⁡u)\,\cdot \frac{1}{5}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{8}{5}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{0}(\operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u-\operatorname{cos}⁡u)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{8}{5}(\operatorname{sec}⁡u-\operatorname{sin}⁡u){|}_{-\pi /3}^{0} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}(\operatorname{sec}⁡0-\operatorname{sin}⁡0)-\frac{8}{5}(\operatorname{sec}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})) \\  & =\frac{8}{5}(1-0)-\frac{8}{5}(2+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{8}{5}-\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{5}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x. \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-(\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}$ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}(2-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x(2-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =(2\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(0+1) \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}-1\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}(3-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x(3-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =(3\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(0+1) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identities $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cot}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡2x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.$ 

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{6}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ |

Therefore, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡u}{2}{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cot}⁡x(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x-2\int \operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+C \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{csc}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

We use the identity $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}3\operatorname{sec}⁡2x{cos}^{2}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.$ 

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{6}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ |

Therefore, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(sin\,(\frac{\pi }{3})-sin\,(0)) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we use the identity $\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡3x}=\operatorname{sec}⁡3x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}\frac{9}{{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}9{(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)})}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}9{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =9{\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=3x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.$ 

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=3x.$

| $x$ | $\frac{\pi }{12}$ | $\frac{\pi }{9}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\frac{\pi }{4}$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ |

Therefore, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}9{\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =9{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡u\,\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u \\  & =3{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{tan}⁡u{|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3} \\  & =3(\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =3(\sqrt{3}-1) \\  & =3\sqrt{3}-3.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
